summary: UCP is a checkout protocol on existing card rails, so most rules land where they already do: the business is merchant of record, its PSP handles authentication, AML screening and disputes, and card and payment-services law decides liability. The new questions are consent (who approved what, which the trusted UI or an AP2 mandate records), AI transparency, and the data a platform sees. UCP checkout runs in the US today; Google says Australia and Canada follow next year and named the UK on 2026-05-20 without a date. Rows are dated; check each source.

rows.text: UCP checkouts on Google are card payments with the business as merchant of record, so credit card disputes follow Regulation Z: unauthorized use means use without actual, implied or apparent authority, and liability is capped at $50. Whether an agent acting outside the buyer's wishes had apparent authority is untested.

For debit-funded payments, Regulation E excludes transfers by someone the consumer gave the access device to, until notice. A buyer who lets an agent pay may carry that loss until they withdraw authority.

A Federal Register search of CFPB documents for AI agents since 2025-01-01 (run 2026-10-20) found no rule or proposal; no federal statute specific to AI shopping agents was found (unverified). A senator's letter dated 2026-02-03 asked Google about data sharing and upselling in Gemini checkout built on UCP.

California's CCPA regulations took effect 2026-01-01; a business that uses automated decisionmaking technology for a significant decision must meet the ADMT requirements by 2027-01-01 (section 7200(b)). Checkout data shared with an agent platform and signals such as buyer IP are personal information.
UCP has no AML or sanctions layer of its own; screening stays with the merchant's PSP and the card networks. OFAC obligations apply as for any card payment.

Remote card payments need strong customer authentication with dynamic linking under the RTS on SCA. UCP's authentication extension carries 3DS2 device data collection and challenges as actions; the PSP owns the 3DS state.
PSD2 requires payer consent to the specific transaction and caps payer liability for unauthorized ones. The trusted UI confirmation, or an AP2 checkout mandate, is the evidence of consent.

AI Act Article 50 transparency applies from 2026-08-02: a buyer must know they deal with an AI system. Generative systems placed on the market before 2026-08-02 have until 2026-12-02 to meet the Article 50(2) marking duty (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744). A shopping agent is not high-risk by default.
GDPR applies to buyer data in checkouts, identity linking and signals; the UCP overview says PII and payment data must follow PCI DSS and GDPR guidance.

Under the Payment Services Regulations 2017 a payment is authorized only with payer consent (regulation 67), and payer liability for misappropriated instruments is capped at GBP 35 (regulation 77). Google said on 2026-05-20 that UCP checkout would reach the UK after Canada and Australia; no UK date was published as of 2026-10-20.
HM Treasury's consultation (2026-07-14 to 2026-10-06) asks how authentication, consent and liability should adapt for agentic payments; no response yet.
No AI statute; the FCA applies existing rules and will consider with HM Treasury whether agentic payments need changes.
The Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 amends UK GDPR rules on automated decision-making.

No agent-specific payment liability rule was found. Google said on 2026-05-20 that UCP checkout would roll out in Canada in the coming months; its Merchant Center help (read 2026-10-20) now says Australia and Canada follow next year.
PIPEDA governs private-sector personal information such as checkout and identity-linking data.
The Retail Payment Activities Act has required PSPs to keep risk management and safeguarding frameworks since 2025-09-08; it applies to the merchant's PSP, not to UCP itself.

MAS's E-Payments User Protection Guidelines set liability for unauthorized transactions and duties for erroneous ones on protected accounts. Their liability apportionment does not apply to credit, charge or debit cards issued in Singapore, which follow the ABS Code of Practice for Banks. The Guidelines do not address agents. No UCP deployment in Singapore was found.
MAS Guidelines on AI Risk Management (issued 2026-10-07, effective 2027-10-07) name agentic AI systems and apply to financial institutions, such as PSPs, that use them.
The Personal Data Protection Act 2012 governs the collection, use and disclosure of personal data by organizations, which covers buyer data in checkouts and identity linking.

Visa's rules (since 2025-10-18) set requirements for Agentic Payment Providers. Visa defines one as the provider of an app that a cardholder uses to carry out tasks on the cardholder's behalf and that meets all of the following conditions. It can search, discover and buy once it receives the cardholder's payment instruction and verification, can undertake an Agentic Transaction, and can be used at more than one merchant. It transmits an EMV payment token, which it also stores when it pays with a stored credential, and passes that token to the merchant to complete the purchase through the merchant's acquirer. It takes no part in authorization, clearing or settlement. Whether a given UCP agent qualifies depends on those conditions.

Visa's rules govern Visa and its member institutions and yield to applicable law. A provider that qualifies must enroll in Visa Intelligent Commerce and register with Visa, directly or via an Agentic Payment Enabler. Within Visa's system, the cardholder is then responsible for its actions in an Agentic Transaction as if the cardholder had initiated it.

Visa calls none of its agent rules a liability shift and adds no agent-specific dispute condition or fee; its April 2026 US interchange schedule has no agentic category. It does require issuers to pay for Agentic Transactions made under a cardholder's payment instructions and not to block them wholesale. From 2026-10-24 it also accepts an Agentic Payment Provider's login ID among the evidence that can defeat a card-absent fraud dispute. Worldpay (2026-07-30) says no liability shift exists yet: tokenized agent payments generally follow existing tokenized-transaction rules for fraud, while disputes short of fraud are unsettled.

Mastercard says standard chargeback rights apply to agentic transactions. The 2026-06-02 Mastercard Rules add no agent-specific liability rule. They require pass-through wallet operators and checkout facilitators in Agent Pay to follow the Mastercard Agent Pay Program Standards. A web search on 2026-10-19 found no public copy of those standards.
EMVCo published a draft EMV Agentic Payments framework on 2026-09-01; UCP carries 3DS2 through actions but does not re-specify EMV 3DS.

The checkout spec says a business does not need PCI DSS compliance to accept cards through the checkout capability, because it receives tokens; a business that accepts the pan credential type is back in scope.
